text:
Morgan Frost is doing what he does: making plays for other people. He has 12 points in 17 games, 8 of them assists, and 6 on the power play. Two more helpers against Anaheim, and he has now passed 200 career points. His shooting sits right at the league average, so nothing here is borrowed.

The style is the interesting part. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 61 percent of his entries, and 61 percent of his shots come off the rush. He is most dangerous in the seconds after Calgary wins the puck back. Evolving-Hockey adds the context that keeps his raw numbers modest: his teammates last season were in the bottom 7 percent by impact, and he was still worth 1.7 wins.

Yardbarker asked this week what the Flames should do with him, which is a fair question on a team still sorting out its future. His ice time has dipped about a minute a night over his last ten. Watch whether that trend continues; he has done enough to deserve the opposite.
headline: Frost keeps setting the table in Calgary
